---
title: "How names rise and fall"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
    collapse = TRUE,
    comment = "#>"
)
```

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(babynamesIL)
library(tidyverse)
theme_set(theme_bw())
```

Most names rise to one peak and fall again. This article measures how long that takes, sorts every name into one
of six shapes, and checks with k-means clustering whether the shapes miss any behavior. The web app shows the
same shapes and numbers on its [Rise and fall page](https://babynames.lifshitz.xyz/?page=rise), and the shape of
each name on its name page; the code here and the app's (`web/lib.js`) follow the same rules and are checked
against the same numbers.

A note on the data: CBS counts Israeli residents in the population register (as of April 2025) by year of birth,
under their current first name. The early years therefore also include people who immigrated later and people who
changed their name. "Babies" below is short for that.

## The curve of a name

For each name and sex in a sector, the curve is the name's share of the listed babies of that sector and sex each
year, averaged over 5 years (centered; the first and last years are repeated at the ends), and divided by its own
maximum, so every curve peaks at 1. Only names given to 50 or more babies in their top year are used. "Half its
peak" is 0.5 on this curve.

```{r curves}
years <- min(babynamesIL$year):max(babynamesIL$year)
min_top <- 50
edge <- 3 # a peak in the first or last 3 years is not taken as an inner peak

smooth5 <- function(v) {
    n <- length(v)
    idx <- pmin(pmax(outer(seq_len(n), -2:2, `+`), 1), n)
    rowMeans(matrix(v[idx], n))
}

shares <- babynamesIL %>%
    group_by(sector, sex, year) %>%
    mutate(share = n / sum(n)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(sector, sex, name, year, n, share) %>%
    complete(nesting(sector, sex, name), year = years, fill = list(n = 0, share = 0))

curves <- shares %>%
    group_by(sector, sex, name) %>%
    filter(max(n) >= min_top) %>%
    arrange(year, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    summarise(top = max(n), x = list(smooth5(share) / max(smooth5(share))), .groups = "drop")
count(curves, sector)
```

## Six shapes

Each name gets one shape, by these rules, in this order:

1. **Comeback** or **camel** (two waves): the curve has a dip (away from the first and last 5 years) below half of the
   lower of the highs on its two sides, and that lower high is at least a quarter of the peak. It is a comeback
   if the first year is already at half the first high (the name did not rise into it within the data), otherwise
   a camel. When a curve has several dips, the deepest one (relative to its lower high) counts.
2. **Stable**: never below a third of its peak.
3. **Still rising**: peak in the last 3 years.
4. **Declining since `r min(years)`**: peak in the first 3 years.
5. **Bell**: the rest, one peak inside the years.

The span of a name is measured on the same curve. **Rise**: years from the first year at half the peak to the
peak. **Fall**: years from the peak to the last year at half the peak. Each is measured only when the peak is at
least 3 years inside the data and that side crosses half inside it, so names cut by the first or last year do not
pull the numbers down.

```{r shapes}
shape_levels <- c("bell", "still rising", "declining since 1949", "stable", "comeback", "camel")

deepest_dip <- function(x) {
    n <- length(x)
    pre <- cummax(x)
    post <- rev(cummax(rev(x)))
    m <- 6:(n - 5)
    lo <- pmin(pre[m - 1], post[m + 1])
    ok <- lo >= 1 / 4
    if (!any(ok)) {
        return(NULL)
    }
    r <- ifelse(ok, x[m] / pmax(lo, 1e-12), Inf)
    low <- m[which.min(r)]
    list(depth = min(r), low = low, high1 = which.max(x[1:(low - 1)]), high2 = low + which.max(x[(low + 1):n]))
}

shape_of <- function(x) {
    n <- length(x)
    p <- which.max(x)
    d <- deepest_dip(x)
    if (!is.null(d) && d$depth < 1 / 2) {
        return(if (x[1] >= x[d$high1] / 2) "comeback" else "camel")
    }
    if (min(x) >= 1 / 3) {
        return("stable")
    }
    if (p > n - edge) {
        return("still rising")
    }
    if (p <= edge) {
        return("declining since 1949")
    }
    "bell"
}

spans_of <- function(x) {
    n <- length(x)
    p <- which.max(x)
    l <- p
    r <- p
    while (l > 1 && x[l - 1] >= 0.5) l <- l - 1
    while (r < n && x[r + 1] >= 0.5) r <- r + 1
    inner <- p > edge && p <= n - edge
    tibble(
        peak = years[p], from = years[l], to = years[r],
        rise = if (inner && l > 1) p - l else NA_integer_,
        fall = if (inner && r < n) r - p else NA_integer_
    )
}

dyn <- curves %>%
    mutate(shape = factor(map_chr(x, shape_of), levels = shape_levels), sp = map(x, spans_of)) %>%
    unnest(sp)

dyn %>%
    count(sector, shape) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = sector, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
    knitr::kable()
```

```{r checks, include = FALSE}
# the same numbers as web/check.mjs, so the app and this article cannot drift apart
n_shape <- function(s) as.integer(table(dyn$shape[dyn$sector == s]))
stopifnot(
    identical(n_shape("Jewish"), c(596L, 119L, 94L, 27L, 64L, 37L)),
    identical(n_shape("Muslim"), c(303L, 59L, 16L, 14L, 13L, 19L))
)
one <- function(nm, sx) filter(dyn, sector == "Jewish", name == nm, sex == sx)
stopifnot(
    one("יוסי", "M")$shape == "bell", one("יוסי", "M")$peak == 1977,
    one("יוסי", "M")$rise == 9, one("יוסי", "M")$fall == 13,
    one("יהודה", "M")$shape == "comeback", one("מאיה", "F")$shape == "camel",
    one("משה", "M")$shape == "stable", one("רחל", "F")$shape == "declining since 1949",
    one("אריאל", "M")$shape == "still rising"
)
```

Every name as one row, grouped by shape and ordered by peak year. The diagonal in "bell" is the procession
of fashions: each name has its turn, and most turns are short.

```{r heatmap}
heat_plot <- function(s) {
    dyn %>%
        filter(sector == s) %>%
        arrange(shape, peak, name) %>%
        group_by(shape) %>%
        mutate(row = row_number()) %>%
        ungroup() %>%
        mutate(year = list(years)) %>%
        select(shape, row, x, year) %>%
        unnest(c(x, year)) %>%
        ggplot(aes(year, row, fill = x)) +
        geom_raster() +
        scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "darkblue", limits = c(0, 1), name = "share of\nits peak") +
        scale_y_reverse(expand = c(0, 0)) +
        scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
        facet_grid(shape ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
        labs(x = "year of birth", y = NULL, title = sprintf("%s  n = %d", s, sum(dyn$sector == s))) +
        theme(
            axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
            strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, size = 7, margin = margin(0, 3, 0, 3)), panel.spacing.y = unit(2, "pt")
        )
}
```

```{r heatmap-jewish, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 9}
heat_plot("Jewish")
```

```{r heatmap-muslim, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
heat_plot("Muslim")
```

The biggest names of the four less common shapes:

```{r examples}
dyn %>%
    filter(sector %in% c("Jewish", "Muslim"), shape %in% c("stable", "comeback", "camel", "still rising")) %>%
    group_by(sector, shape) %>%
    slice_max(top, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    summarise(names = paste(name, collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop") %>%
    knitr::kable()
```

Some of these sit on the edge of a rule. A name with a low but sizable level in 1949 and one big rise later can
count as a comeback (בן, ניקול), and a one-year spike can make a second high (שמחה, in the 1990s). In the
Muslim sector the early years have few listed babies (`r babynamesIL %>% filter(sector == "Muslim", year == 1949) %>% pull(n) %>% sum()` in 1949),
so some early dips there (ג'יהאד, פארס) may be noise, and several Muslim camel curves are jagged.

## How long a rise and fall takes

```{r spans}
med <- function(v) {
    v <- v[!is.na(v)]
    if (length(v) < 20) {
        return("too few names")
    }
    sprintf("%s (%s-%s), n=%d", format(median(v)), round(quantile(v, 0.25)), round(quantile(v, 0.75)), length(v))
}
dyn %>%
    group_by(sector) %>%
    summarise(
        span = med(if_else(!is.na(rise) & !is.na(fall), rise + fall + 1L, NA_integer_)),
        rise = med(rise), fall = med(fall)
    ) %>%
    relocate(span, .after = fall) %>%
    knitr::kable(caption = "Median years (middle half of the names), and the number of names measured. Span: years at or above half the peak, for names with both sides measured.")
```

```{r span-checks, include = FALSE}
span_med <- function(s, col) median(dyn[[col]][dyn$sector == s], na.rm = TRUE)
both <- dyn %>% filter(!is.na(rise), !is.na(fall))
stopifnot(
    span_med("Jewish", "rise") == 7, span_med("Jewish", "fall") == 10,
    median(both$rise[both$sector == "Jewish"] + both$fall[both$sector == "Jewish"] + 1) == 18,
    span_med("Muslim", "rise") == 6, span_med("Muslim", "fall") == 8,
    median(both$rise[both$sector == "Muslim"] + both$fall[both$sector == "Muslim"] + 1) == 15
)
```

A typical name takes about 7 years to climb from half its peak to the peak, and 10 years to fall back to half
(Jewish sector); Muslim names are faster on both sides. The fall is slower than the rise for most names, and
names that rise slowly also tend to fall slowly:

```{r rise-fall}
both %>%
    filter(sector %in% c("Jewish", "Muslim")) %>%
    group_by(sector) %>%
    summarise(
        names = n(), fall_slower = mean(fall > rise), fall_faster = mean(fall < rise),
        spearman_rho = cor(rise, fall, method = "spearman")
    ) %>%
    knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

```{r ecdf, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 3.5}
dyn %>%
    filter(sector %in% c("Jewish", "Muslim")) %>%
    pivot_longer(c(rise, fall), names_to = "side", values_to = "years_") %>%
    filter(!is.na(years_)) %>%
    mutate(side = factor(side, c("rise", "fall"), c("rise: half the peak to the peak", "fall: the peak to half"))) %>%
    ggplot(aes(years_, color = sector)) +
    stat_ecdf(geom = "step") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(Jewish = "black", Muslim = "coral3")) +
    facet_wrap(~side) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 45)) +
    labs(x = "years", y = "fraction of names")
```

Lining up the bell names on their peak year shows the typical shape. The median curve is at or above
half its peak from about 8 years before the peak to 11 after (Jewish). It does not fall to zero: 20 years after
the peak the median name is still at about a quarter of its peak, which is why the whole curve, tails included,
spans about 40 years.

```{r aligned, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 3.5}
aligned <- dyn %>%
    filter(sector %in% c("Jewish", "Muslim"), shape == "bell") %>%
    mutate(p = peak - min(years) + 1) %>%
    select(sector, name, sex, p, x) %>%
    crossing(offset = -40:40) %>%
    mutate(i = p + offset) %>%
    filter(i >= 1, i <= length(years)) %>%
    mutate(v = map2_dbl(x, i, ~ .x[.y])) %>%
    group_by(sector, offset) %>%
    filter(n() >= 30) %>%
    summarise(
        q10 = quantile(v, 0.1), q25 = quantile(v, 0.25), q50 = median(v),
        q75 = quantile(v, 0.75), q90 = quantile(v, 0.9), .groups = "drop"
    )

ggplot(aligned, aes(offset)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q10, ymax = q90), fill = "gray85") +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75), fill = "gray65") +
    geom_line(aes(y = q50)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dotted") +
    facet_wrap(~sector) +
    labs(x = "years from the peak", y = "share of its peak")
```

Light band: middle 80% of the names; dark band: middle half; line: median; dotted: half the peak. Only offsets
with at least 30 names are drawn.

### Does the cut-off of 50 babies matter?

Rerunning everything with other cut-offs for the name's top year:

```{r thresholds}
map_dfr(c(100, 50, 30, 20), function(th) {
    shares %>%
        group_by(sector, sex, name) %>%
        filter(max(n) >= th) %>%
        arrange(year, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
        summarise(x = list(smooth5(share) / max(smooth5(share))), .groups = "drop") %>%
        mutate(shape = factor(map_chr(x, shape_of), levels = shape_levels), sp = map(x, spans_of)) %>%
        unnest(sp) %>%
        group_by(sector) %>%
        summarise(
            top_year_at_least = th, names = n(),
            span = median((rise + fall + 1)[!is.na(rise) & !is.na(fall)]),
            rise = median(rise, na.rm = TRUE), fall = median(fall, na.rm = TRUE),
            shapes = paste(as.integer(table(shape)), collapse = " / ")
        )
}) %>%
    arrange(factor(sector, c("Jewish", "Muslim", "Christian-Arab", "Druze")), desc(top_year_at_least)) %>%
    knitr::kable(caption = paste("Shapes:", paste(shape_levels, collapse = " / ")))
```

The spans hardly move. Christian-Arab and Druze names enter only at lower cut-offs, where half of a name's peak is
close to the CBS floor of 5 babies a year, so their curves are noisy.

The 5-year average itself matters more: on the raw yearly share, the same Jewish names give a median span of 14
years instead of 18, because a single noisy year below half ends the span early, while the average lowers and
widens sharp peaks. Both are reasonable; the numbers above use the average.

## Does clustering find other shapes?

The rules were written by looking at the curves, so they could miss a behavior nobody looked for. k-means on the
same curves (calendar years, each scaled to its peak) checks that.

```{r kmeans5}
km <- function(X, k) {
    set.seed(1)
    kmeans(X, k, nstart = 20, iter.max = 100)
}
centre_peak <- function(fit) years[apply(fit$centers, 1, which.max)]

kmeans_table <- function(s, k) {
    d <- filter(dyn, sector == s)
    fit <- km(do.call(rbind, d$x), k)
    tibble(cluster = fit$cluster, shape = d$shape) %>%
        mutate(centre_peak = centre_peak(fit)[cluster]) %>%
        count(centre_peak, cluster, shape) %>%
        pivot_wider(names_from = shape, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
        arrange(centre_peak)
}
kmeans_table("Jewish", 5) %>% knitr::kable(caption = "Jewish, k = 5: clusters (by the peak year of their centre) by shape")
```

With 5 clusters, k-means mostly cuts the names by the years they peaked, not by shape: on calendar years the
timing of the peak outweighs everything else. The one cluster that follows shape is the traditional names that were
high all along: it holds all the stable names and many of the comebacks. More clusters keep improving the
fit, with no clear elbow:

```{r wss, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 3}
map_dfr(c("Jewish", "Muslim"), function(s) {
    X <- do.call(rbind, filter(dyn, sector == s)$x)
    tot <- sum(scale(X, scale = FALSE)^2)
    tibble(sector = s, k = 2:12, wss = map_dbl(2:12, ~ km(X, .x)$tot.withinss / tot))
}) %>%
    ggplot(aes(k, wss, color = sector)) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_point() +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(Jewish = "black", Muslim = "coral3")) +
    expand_limits(y = 0) +
    labs(y = "within-cluster sum of squares\n(share of k = 1)")
```

With many clusters (about 16 names each), most cluster centres are still one rise and fall at different times.
The centres that are not (more than one stretch at or above half their maximum, or never below a third of it)
hold the shapes the rules name, plus one the rules leave in "stable", "bell" and "declining": a decline to
a lasting floor.

```{r kmeans-many, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5}
stretches <- function(v) {
    m <- v >= max(v) / 2
    m[1] + sum(!head(m, -1) & tail(m, -1))
}
many <- map_dfr(c("Jewish", "Muslim"), function(s) {
    d <- filter(dyn, sector == s)
    X <- do.call(rbind, d$x)
    fit <- km(X, round(nrow(X) / 16))
    odd <- which(apply(fit$centers, 1, function(v) stretches(v) > 1 || min(v) >= max(v) / 3))
    map_dfr(odd, function(j) {
        members <- d[fit$cluster == j, ]
        tibble(
            sector = s, cluster = j, centre_peak = years[which.max(fit$centers[j, ])], names = nrow(members),
            shapes = paste(names(sort(table(droplevels(members$shape)), decreasing = TRUE)), collapse = ", "),
            examples = paste(head(members$name[order(-members$top)], 6), collapse = ", "),
            centre = list(fit$centers[j, ])
        )
    })
})
many %>%
    select(-centre) %>%
    arrange(sector, centre_peak) %>%
    knitr::kable(caption = "Clusters whose centre is not one rise and fall, and the shapes of their names (most common first)")

many %>%
    arrange(sector, centre_peak) %>%
    mutate(panel = factor(sprintf("%s %d: %s", substr(sector, 1, 1), centre_peak, names), levels = unique(sprintf("%s %d: %s", substr(sector, 1, 1), centre_peak, names)))) %>%
    mutate(year = list(years)) %>%
    unnest(c(centre, year)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(year, centre, color = sector)) +
    geom_line() +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(Jewish = "black", Muslim = "coral3")) +
    facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 6) +
    expand_limits(y = 0) +
    labs(y = "cluster centre (share of peak)", x = "year of birth") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Panel titles: sector, peak year of the centre, number of names.

### Clustering the shapes themselves

To ask k-means about shape alone, each curve is lined up on its peak year and cut to 15 years on each side. Only
names peaking in `r years[16]`-`r years[length(years) - 15]` have that whole window inside the data.

```{r aligned-kmeans, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6}
W <- 15
win <- dyn %>%
    filter(sector %in% c("Jewish", "Muslim")) %>%
    mutate(p = peak - min(years) + 1) %>%
    filter(p > W, p <= length(years) - W)
count(win, sector, shape) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = sector, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
    knitr::kable()

aligned_centres <- map_dfr(c(Jewish = 12, Muslim = 6) %>% imap(~ list(s = .y, k = .x)), function(a) {
    d <- filter(win, sector == a$s)
    X <- do.call(rbind, map2(d$x, d$p, ~ .x[(.y - W):(.y + W)]))
    fit <- km(X, a$k)
    half <- apply(fit$centers, 1, function(v) range(which(v >= max(v) / 2)) - W - 1)
    tibble(
        sector = a$s, cluster = seq_len(a$k), names = as.integer(table(factor(fit$cluster, seq_len(a$k)))),
        lo = half[1, ], hi = half[2, ], centre = map(seq_len(a$k), ~ unname(fit$centers[.x, ]))
    )
})
aligned_centres %>%
    arrange(sector, hi - lo) %>%
    mutate(panel = factor(sprintf("%s %+d to %+d: %d", substr(sector, 1, 1), lo, hi, names), levels = unique(sprintf("%s %+d to %+d: %d", substr(sector, 1, 1), lo, hi, names)))) %>%
    mutate(offset = list(-W:W)) %>%
    unnest(c(centre, offset)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(offset, centre, color = sector)) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dotted") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(Jewish = "black", Muslim = "coral3")) +
    facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 6) +
    expand_limits(y = 0) +
    labs(x = "years from the peak", y = "cluster centre (share of peak)") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Panel titles: sector, the years from the peak where the centre is at or above half its maximum, number of names;
ordered from narrow to wide. Every centre is a single rise and fall. They differ in width, from a few years on each
side to more than the whole window, and in which side is slower: most fall more slowly than they rise, a few rise
slowly and drop fast. The widths form a continuum rather than separate groups, so the six shapes, with the rise
and fall times, describe the names well: almost every name is one rise and fall of some width, and a minority
come back.
